root_cause.text: In futex FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE_PI, the non-top waiter requeue path called rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock() without first checking whether the waiter task already owned the target PI rt_mutex, so task_blocks_on_rt_mutex() could return -EDEADLK before initializing waiter->task and remove_waiter() later dereferenced that NULL field.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message state that for “a non-top waiter that already owns the target PI futex, task_blocks_on_rt_mutex() returns -EDEADLK before setting waiter->task” and then “remove_waiter() in rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock() dereferences the NULL waiter->task”; the patch adds an explicit pre-check in kernel/futex/requeue.c, `if (rt_mutex_owner(&pi_state->pi_mutex) == this->task) { ret = -EDEADLK; break; }`, before calling `rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Detect and abort self-deadlock during PI futex requeue when a waiter already owns the target rt_mutex.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added before calling rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock() in futex_requeue(): if rt_mutex_owner(&pi_state->pi_mutex) equals this->task, the code sets ret to -EDEADLK and breaks out of the loop, with an accompanying comment noting a self-deadlock case for a non-top waiter owning the PI futex.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents attempting to proxy-lock a PI futex for a task that already owns that rt_mutex, detecting a self-deadlock condition early and returning -EDEADLK instead of proceeding into an invalid lock acquisition path.

grouping_result.intent: Detect and abort self-deadlock during PI futex requeue when a waiter already owns the target rt_mutex.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds self-deadlock detection in the PI futex requeue path when the waiter already owns the target rt_mutex, preventing the rt_mutex proxy-lock path from hitting the uninitialized waiter state that led to the NULL dereference.

candidates.rationale: This call is the direct trigger of the vulnerability: in the non-top waiter requeue path it was invoked without first checking whether this->task already owned the target PI rt_mutex. That allowed rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock() to hit the self-deadlock path (-EDEADLK) before waiter initialization, leading to later dereference of an uninitialized waiter->task.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call initiated proxy locking for a requeued non-top waiter without first verifying that the waiter task did not already own the target PI rt_mutex. In the self-deadlock case, rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock() could return -EDEADLK before waiter->task was initialized, which later led to a NULL dereference in remove_waiter().

In the requeue-PI loop, after `get_pi_state(pi_state)` and `futex_requeue_pi_prepare(this, pi_state)`, the code directly calls `ret = rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock(&pi_state->pi_mutex, this->rt_waiter, this->task);` with no prior check whether `this->task` already owns `pi_state->pi_mutex`. That is exactly the vulnerable construct described in the root cause: invoking `rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock()` without first checking for self-ownership can make it return `-EDEADLK` before waiter initialization is complete. The error path immediately below confirms the code expects such failures generically: `else { ... this->pi_state = NULL; put_pi_state(pi_state); futex_requeue_pi_complete(this, ret); ... }`, but there is no added guard that would prevent the deadlock/self-owner case before calling `rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock()`. Since the fix would require an explicit ownership check before this call, and no such check is present anywhere in the shown logic, the fix is not present.
